answer: The tundra escrow freezes every token a new agent earns and thaws it at 1% per day, so a full payout needs 100 quiet days. A farm that bursts 10,000 tokens and runs finds 97% still under ice, worthless. Spoofing one clean history costs 30 days of uptime at roughly $12 of API fees for a payout capped near $30. Each thawed batch keeps its timestamp, and the ledger roots every schedule in a lotus hash: a farm spends in one spike while an honest agent drops walnut-sized steady batches, so a burst shows up as a red line against the known curve before its tokens ever touch a market.
